abstract: In practice, due to the difficulty in obtaining the precise probability distributions of the uncertain variables, the stochastic reliability-based design optimization (RBDO) methods can hardly be effective in various cases. On contrary, the variation intervals of the uncertain parameter can be relatively easily achieved. In terms of this condition, an efficient sequential optimization and reliability assessment method of decoupled scheme is developed in this paper for the non-probabilistic RBDO (NRBDO) of electrical machines with interval uncertainty.

articleTitle: Novel Analysis Method Using Analytical and Numerical Methods for AC Copper Loss of IPMSM Considering Inverter Carrier Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: To analyze AC copper loss of the electric vehicle (EV) motors accurately, it is calculated using the finite element method (FEM) after extracting the inverter-fed current (IFC) by space vector PWM. However, the harmonic waves of the IFC are different at each operating point, it takes a long time to analyze AC copper loss using the FEM. Thus, it is difficult to calculate AC copper loss at the entire efficiency map. To overcome the problem, this paper proposes an AC copper loss calculation method according to i<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>, iq and operating speed by considering inverter carrier harmonics. Proposed method uses both analytical and numerical methods. The validity of the proposed method is proved by comparing of analysis time and accuracy between this method and the fully FEM.

articleTitle: Research on Permanent Magnet-Induction Magnetic Screw for Wave Energy Conversion
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A new type of permanent magnet-induction magnetic screw (PMI-MS), as a linear rotary actuator (LRA) with high thrust density and high energy conversion efficiency compared with the traditional direct-drive wave energy conversion (DD-WEC), is proposed and applied in wave energy conversion (WEC). The proposed PMI-MS adopts the method of quasi-Halbach magnetization array and hybrid excitation to overcome the shortcomings of the non-adjustable thrust of the permanent magnet magnetic screw (PM-MS) and the low thrust density of the induction magnetic screw (I-MS). At the same time, the special structure of adjacent teeth with different heights on the mover can improve the electromagnetic thrust generated by the electric excitation, thereby further improving the thrust adjustment capability and thrust density of the PMI-MS. Compared with conventional PMI-MS, it has higher thrust density and higher wave energy conversion efficiency compared with the wave energy linear generators. To optimize and design the PMI-MS, analytical methods and global optimization algorithms are adopted. Finally, finite element simulations are used to verify that the proposed PMI-MS has higher thrust density.

articleTitle: Hysteresis Modeling and Measurement of Oriented Silicon Steel Under PWM Excitation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, method for modeling and measuring oriented silicon steel sheet excited by pulse width modulation (PWM) signal is proposed in this paper. The magnetic property test platform of oriented silicon steel sheet excited by PWM power is established. According to the experimental data of magnetization mechanism and magnetic properties of silicon steel sheet, combined with Preisach model, the hysteresis model of silicon steel sheet under PWM excitation is established. It provides an accurate material parameter model for calculating the magnetic field distribution of laminated iron core of product grade transformer.

articleTitle: Research on Magnetic and Stress-induced Anisotropy of Silicon Steel Considering Magnetic Domain Deflection
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In the process of reducing the vibration and noise of transformers and motors, the compressive stress of the clamp and the shell will cause magnetic and stress-induced anisotropy, and affect the magnetostrictive strain of the core materials. This paper proposed a free energy model of silicon steel based on the principle of minimizing magnetic domain energy. The model can simulate the deflection path of the magnetic domain under external magnetic field and stress by calculating the distribution of the energy extreme point. The basic magnetization curves of silicon steel materials under different stresses are simulated by the free energy model, which verifies the accuracy of the proposed silicon steel free energy model.

articleTitle: GPU-Based Near Real-Time Estimation of the Human Body Penetrating Low-Frequency Magnetic Fields Using Free Space Field Measurements
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Low-frequency magnetic fields emanated by wireless power transfer systems expose human beings in their vicinity and induce electric fields into the biological tissues. These potentially harmful induced body-internal electric fields should not exceed the ICNIRP recommended strength limits. The Scalar Potential Finite Difference scheme can be utilized to determine these induced electric fields and thus to assess the human exposure but requires the magnetic flux density distribution in the volume of the exposed body as input. The goal of this work is to determine this magnetic flux density distribution from a few in-situ free-space measurements using graphics processing unit (GPU) accelerated interpolation schemes in near real-time. A single NVIDIA Tesla A100 GPU allows a magnetic flux density distribution reconstruction with an ICNIRP recommended human voxel model resolution of 2 mm in less than 1 second based on 19 sampling points using radial basis functions.

articleTitle: Self-Check Function of Double-Layer Approach in Multiply-Connected Problem
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The Double-Layer Approach possesses superior features for the analysis of static magnetic problems. In this paper, as a novelty, we introduce the Self-Check Function, an inherent feature in the double-layer BEM, which enables proof of the correctness of the solutions of the governing BIE. Thanks to the Self-Check Function, we can easily prove the solution of BIE by tracking the magnetic field. When analyzing the multiply-connected problem in magnetostatic, it is obligatory to use the cut-surface. There appear two kinds of double-layers: one on the surface of magnetic body and the other on the cut-surface within the exciting current loop. Utilizing the Ampere's circuital integral law, we introduce the novel, unified exciting double-layer on the cut-surface, controlled by the Self-Check Function. Using the Self-Check Function, we solve a typical multiply-connected problem and demonstrate that the unified exciting double-layer works well.

articleTitle: Effects of Dynamic Constraint on Stator End-winding Stress for Large Traction Motor Based on 3-D Magnetic-structural FEM
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The operating environment of traction motor is quite different from that of traditional motor, which may affect the dynamic response of vibration and stress caused by the complex coupling electromagnetic force and mechanical constraints at the end of stator winding. In this paper, the influence of dynamic constraints on the end stress of stator winding is studied for a large traction motor with 2.8 MW rated power. The magnetic-structure model was established, and the stress response of the end winding was determined by three-dimensional finite element method. Set winding asymmetric constraints to simulate the impact of dynamic constraints. The results show that when the end winding is asymmetrically constrained, the maximum displacement value of the winding is twice as large as that of the complete constraint, and the maximum position appears at the winding nose. Under asymmetric constraints, the radial displacement is much larger than the circumferential displacement, about 3.6 times. This is beneficial to the research and understanding of fault mechanism of large traction motor end winding.

articleTitle: Frequency Sensitivity Analysis of Eddy Current system in Voltage Source Problems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-order frequency-sensitivity analysis of a linear eddy-current system coupled with voltage-driven circuit and shows its validity through two numerical examples. In this field-circuit coupled system, an exciting coil is connected to a voltage source and an external circuit in series. An analytic sensitivity formula for the sensitivity analysis is derived by differentiating the variational equation of the coupled system with respect to frequency. An nth order frequency sensitivity is obtained from the lower-order one. The numerical analysis of the frequency-sensitivity is performed using a commercial finite-element analysis software. A cylindrical wire and an induction heating system are numerically tested to validate the frequency-sensitivity analysis.

articleTitle: Analysis of IPMSM unbalance characteristics through 3-phase 2-channel SVPWM Dual Inverter control
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, IPMSM for driving a 300kW electric vehicle with 2 channels of power input terminal is analyzed in conjunction with a motor and an inverter with 2 output terminals to study the characteristics change. The stator winding of IPMSM is made of 2 channels in case one phase of the winding is a fault, and each channel is composed of 3 phase Y connection. In addition, the inverter output terminal for applying power to the motor is also designed with 2 channels. In the two inverter-controlled drives, a difference in current applied to the motor between channels occurs due to a control error. To analyze the characteristics of the motor according to the degree of unbalance, the inverter and the motor are analyzed in combination.

articleTitle: Analysis of Skewing method considering 3-D Electromagnetic Force
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Noise, vibration, and harshness (NVH) in motors degrade the performance and life cycle. Therefore, electromagnetic force of motor should be reduced, which affects NVH. The methods of applying skew to stator or rotor generally focus on radial and tangential force than axial force. However, some skew conditions may generate the unexpected axial force, which has uncertainty in NVH. In this paper, we investigate the 3-D electromagnetic forces according to skew types, which is consisted of step number, stack length and angle between steps, based on the maxwell stress tensor. As a result of analysis, the novel skew condition is proposed, and the comparison of performance in both conventional and proposed model is also present.

articleTitle: Hybrid Method for Calculating Eddy Current Loss in Permanent Magnet with Axial Segment of IPMSM
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid method for calculating permanent magnet (PM) eddy current loss (PMECL) of interior PM synchronous motor (IPMSM) is proposed. PMECL in axial segmented PM of IPMSM driven by pulse width modulation inverter is calculated through a combination of two-dimensional finite element method and analytical method. Using the proposed procedure, PMECL of axial segmented PM is analyzed by operating point and the number of axial segments of PM.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer Coil Design for Interoperability and Tolerance to Misalignment
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this contribution the authors investigate a modular structure of Wireless Power Transfer system specifically dedicated to a quasi-static or dynamic operation mode in an urban environment. The proposed architecture has been simulated by using a commercial software and has proven to be characterized by excellent performances in terms of small interaction between each single module and tolerant to misalignment.

articleTitle: Axisymmetric Coil Design with Improved Inductance Using Geometric Mean Distance Simulation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In systems that transmit power or signals using magnetic fields, such as wireless power transmission, sensors, and RFID, the inductance of the coil has a significant effect on the transmission performance. It is simple to mathematically calculate the inductance of a single filament coil, but there are not many studies on calculating the inductance of a coil having an arbitrary cross section. In this paper, a geometric mean distance simulation was programmed and used to calculate the inductance. The inductance of the rectangular section coil was calculated and verified through finite element simulation, and the aspect ratio of the rectangular section coil with the maximum mutual inductance was obtained. In addition, the shape of the cross-section of the coil having a higher mutual inductance than that of a rectangular-section coil was presented, and the results showed that a coils with right triangular and quarter-elliptical cross-section had a higher mutual inductance.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Transformer Inter-Turn Short-Circuit Faults Based on Field-Circuit Coupling
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Transformer inter-turn short-circuit (ITSC) fault has long been an issue of concern. This paper presents a direct field-circuit coupling method to investigate power transformer ITSC faults, in which the nonlinear arc-in-oil conductance was simultaneously calculated. Using the numerical approach, ITSC faults of a three-phase three-winding power transformer were simulated and analyzed. Results show that, a large circulating current flows through the shorted turns, with the surrounding flux distribution significantly distorted. Moreover, ITSC faults with more shorted turns will result in lower short-circuit current and larger arc voltage, and more arcing fault energy will be released.

articleTitle: Comparison Research on Axial Flux Modulation Generators for Linear-rotary Wave Energy Conversion
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: To improve the performance of generators used for Underwater wave energy converter, This paper proposed a linear-rotary axial flux modulation generator. The operation principle is analyzed. Four generators with different ratio of number of modulation teeth and permanent magnet pole are studied. The performances under no-load and on-load condition are comparison researched. An optimal axial flux modulation generator is obtained.

articleTitle: Computing Cochlear Implant Electrode Interface Impedance based on Electric Field Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Electric field imaging (EFI) is a valuable approach in cochlear implant (CI) research, which is used to study the potential distribution inside the cochlea and examine whether the implanted electrodes are functioning properly. Accurate knowledge of the electrode interface impedance is critical for improving CI performance. A 3D patient-specific CI model was built to simulate EFI using the finite element method (FEM). Intracochlear potentials were recorded by multiple sensing electrodes and the corresponding impedance values were computed. The simulation results were compared with the EFI data obtained from the clinical measurements. The EFI simulated by patient-specific and generic electrode trajectories were also compared. Results showed that the patient-specific trajectory simulations were consistent with the clinical measurements. The impedance value computed in this research has the potential to increase the accuracy of evoked compound action potential (ECAP) simulations.

articleTitle: Analysis of Loss Modeling in Flux-Reversal PM Machine
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Flux-reversal permanent-magnet (FRPM) machine has gained more and more attention in the recent years due to its several advantages, such as simple rotor structure and easy heat management. In this paper, the iron loss either in no-load and on-load condition is modeled, taking the rotational magnetization, DC-biased magnetic induction, minor hysteresis loops, and PWM carrier harmonics into consideration. Then, PM eddy current loss is calculated. Finally, in order to verify the results, two prototype machines are manufactured, and both the no-load and on-load test are conducted. The results show that PM loss in 6/8 FRPM machine with m1 is close to that with m2, while iron loss in 6/8 FRPM machine with m2 is larger than that with m1.

articleTitle: Topology Optimization of IPMSM Using Sequential Linear Programming in Combination with Magnetic Field and Mechanical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Since the interior permanent magnet synchronous motors (IPMSMs) are actively applied to the industrial machines such as EV, the design of high-performance IPMSM is substantially demanded. Further, to protect the deformation of the rotor core in the high speed rotation, the high stiffness should be also considered. In this paper, the topology optimization method of IPMSM using sequential linear programming method in combination with the magnetic field and mechanical analysis is investigated.

articleTitle: A New nalysis Method Based on Lumped Magnetic Circuit Model for Surface Permanent-Magnet Machines with Step-Skewed Rotor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This study proposes a new analysis method based on lumped magnetic-circuit for surface permanent-magnet machine (SPM) with overhang and step-skewed rotor. In SPM machine, the step-skew lowers the torque pulsation and makes the electromotive force sinusoidal, and the overhang structure increases the torque density. A time-consuming three dimensional (3-D) finite element method (FEM) is required to analyze axial components such as step-skew leakage flux and overhang flux. To deal with this problem, a new equivalent lumped magnetic-circuit model for each rotor step considering the axial leakage flux between the steps and the linkage flux by the overhang is introduced. The validity of the proposed method is verified by comparing a two-dimensional and 3-D FEM of skewed, non-skewed, overhang, and non-overhang SPMs.

articleTitle: Thin-Wire EFIE-MoM Formulation for Fast Computational Analysis of Microstrip Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Ahstract- This work adapts the thin-wire approximation to the integro-differential formulation that models electromagnetic wave propagation through thin microstrip metasurfaces. A computationally efficient approach is achieved by reducing a surface current distribution to a filamentary electric current immersed in an effective dielectric medium. Besides, this is a general formulation that can be applied to wire and microstrip structures, even with lumped elements. Finally, this formulation is used to calculate the magnetic field through a magnetic metasurface lens excited by a wire loop. The results obtained agree on the overall behavior with full-wave simulation in commercial software, with almost 33 times faster computational time.

articleTitle: Determination of Equivalent Permeability of Soft Magnetic Composites Considering Manufacturing Process
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A novel evaluation method of the equivalent permeability of soft magnetic composites (SMC) is proposed, referring to the pressing mechanism. Firstly, the microstructure of the SMC is analyzed, and the region between ferromagnetic particles is divided into gaps and pores. An analytical calculation method for two permeability boundaries is derived when the non-ferromagnetic region is completely occupied by gaps or pores. Finally, the accurate homogenized permeability can be determined in terms of composites density and the ratio of gaps and pores which is affected by the manufacturing process parameters during preparation. The proposed method can tentatively predict the magnetic properties of composites, thereby helping select appropriate processing parameters.

articleTitle: Extended Finite Element Method Coupling with Complex Bubble Dynamic Characteristics in Electrostatic Field
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Due to the complex dynamic characteristics of bubbles, it is crucial to research an accurate and rapid method to calculate the electric potential distribution in the liquid. In this paper, an extended finite element method (XFEM) for coupling the bubble dynamic characteristics is proposed. First, the hydrodynamical equation is used to find the velocities at the nodes. Then, the velocity is substituted into the governing equation of the level set function. Finally, the level set function values at the nodes are coupled to the XFEM equations under the electrostatic field to calculate the electric potential distribution in a two-phase flow. By comparison, it is proved that the error of the calculation result between this method and the conventional finite element method coupling fluid dynamics is less than 5%, and the calculation time is saved by two-thirds.

articleTitle: Losses Computation in Double Armored AC Submarine Cables
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: An integral equation formulation already developed by the authors is applied to a conductive geometry characterized by three helically twisted structures. In particular, a suitable geometrical approximation is used for the computation of power losses in double armored AC submarine cables. The proposed approach is validated with FEM simulations.

articleTitle: Dielectric Radome Analysis with a Simplified Nonstandard Path Integral Model
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The nonstandard finite-difference time-domain (NS-FDTD) method is a highly accurate numerical tool, however, it is not suitable for curved-surface objects, as it employs discrete points on orthogonal grids. To this objective, a path integral (PI) model can be considered as a useful means to drastically improve the efficiency of the NS-FDTD algorithm. It has been previously shown that the featured scheme can greatly improve the NS-FDTD competence for curved surface on rough orthogonal grids and PEC objects. In this paper, we analyze a radome with curved dielectric parts and confirm the effectivity of the PI model.

articleTitle: Multiscale Modelling of Materials With Strong Dynamic Hysteresis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Manufacturing electrical machines made of cus-tomized materials, such as soft magnetic composites (SMC) is crucial when pursuing higher energy efficiency and minimized amount of material per machine. To computationally obtain accurate designs of such machines, multiscale modelling methods are needed. This paper focuses on modelling SMC materials with strong macroscopic dynamic hysteresis using the finite element method together with a multiscale method. Furthermore, two different methods for modelling the fields in time are utilized, scrutinized and compared: the time-stepping method (TSM) and the multiharmonic method (MHM). As a novel contribution, this paper aims to show that the MHM results into a more stable numerical solver than the TSM, which may suffer from con-vergence problems due to the ill-posed differential permeability observed at the macroscale.

articleTitle: A Novel V-Shaped Nonoverlapping Stator Wound Field Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, based on the conventional nonoverlapping stator wound field synchronous (N-SWFS) machine, a novel V-shaped-stator-teeth N-SWFS (VN-SWFS) machine is proposed by changing winding configurations and the shape of stator teeth. The operating principle of the proposed machine is explained by analyzing the no-load excitation magnetic flux path. The influence of stator-slots/rotor-teeth combination on VN-SWFS machines is studied through finite-element analysis, the proposed 12/10, 12/11, 12/13, and 12/14 VN-SWFS machines are quantitatively compared in terms of no-load back electromotive force (back-EMF), cogging torque and electromagnetic torque.

articleTitle: Energy Loss in Soft Magnetic Materials under Harmonic Excitation and High Induction
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In order to achieve accurate prediction of soft magnetic material loss in a wide range of frequencies and flux densities, this paper proposes a calculation method based on the loss separation model that can take into account the skin effect of soft magnetic materials and accurately simulate the material losses under harmonic excitation conditions. First, a nonlinear Preisach model is used to calculate the hysteresis loss by fitting the first-order and the second-order slew curve simultaneously. Then, under low flux density and high frequency, the classical loss is obtained by approximating the material's intrinsic structure relationship as linear; under high flux density and high frequency, the fixed-point finite element technique based on the H-B-M magnetic intrinsic structure relationship is introduced into the harmonic finite element calculation to calculate the classical loss under high flux density. Finally, energy loss in the frequency range of 1 kHz and under different harmonic excitation conditions are calculated. It shows that the method in this paper are in good agreement with experimental measurement results, which verifies the accuracy of the method.

articleTitle: Losses Caused by End-region Field in Synchronous Generators at Different Operating Conditions
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: It is challenging to measure losses caused by end-region field in real synchronous generators, because of accessibility and cost. This paper presents a dedicated test setup to emulate the field experienced by clamping structures and stator end core, and validate loss models. Measurements show that the loss model employed has an averaged error of 3.6%. Investigation of a 100 kVA synchronous generator shows that these losses are heavily dependent on operating conditions. The case with Leading PF has the highest loss, and the dominant loss component for all the cases is eddy current loss in clamping structures.

articleTitle: A Novel Electric Field Feature Set of Transmission Line - Tower Air Gaps and Its Application for Insulation Strength Prediction
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Air gap is the main form of external insulation of transmission lines, whose discharge characteristics are closely associated with the spatial electric field distribution between electrodes. This paper defines 83 features to characterize the electric field distribution of transmission tower gaps, which are determined by the original data of hypothetical interelectrode paths and equipotential rings obtained by finite element method. A machine learning model constructed by support vector machine and trained by electric field feature set of 500kV, ±660 kV, and 750 kV transmission line - tower air gaps was used to calculate the switching impulse discharge voltages of ±800 kV and 1000 kV air gaps. The predicted results with different input feature subsets, which were selected by Pearson correlation coefficient, was analyzed and compared with experimental values. The results show that the minimum mean absolute percentage error is only 3.4 % after feature selection. This method is useful to predict long air gap discharge voltage with engineering gap configurations.

articleTitle: Characteristic Analysis and Verification of Electromagnetic Force for Armature of the Electromagnetic Rail Launcher
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, the armature electromagnetic force of the electromagnetic rail launcher is taken as the research object, and the electromagnetic field control equation considering the influence of armature movement velocity and the armature dynamic equation considering the influence of resistance are given. Then, the finite element calculation model of the electromagnetic rail launcher is built, and the correctness of the model is verified by data comparison. Finally, the trapezoidal excitation current is used to further analyze the dynamic characteristics of the armature electromagnetic force under the influence of different factors. The research results have important guiding significance for the study of the dynamic characteristics of the electromagnetic rail launcher under the actual working conditions and the refined design of the pivot rail structure.

articleTitle: An Air Gap Model for Magnetostatic Volume Integral Formulation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents an air gap model for thin air gaps using the magnetostatic volume integral method. The thin air gap is considered as a surface region with a numerical treatment instead of a volume region to avoid having a thin mesh that could lead to long computations. An application to a current transformer is reported to show its accuracy.

articleTitle: A Study on Performance Improvement by Reducing Axial Force of Double-Layer Spoke-type PMSM with Core Skew Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Unlike general spoke-type PMSMs, double-layer spoke-type PMSMs can utilize high reluctance torque by increasing the difference between d-axis and q-axis reluctance. However, as the difference in magnetic resistance increases, vibration and noise are generated, which adversely affects the mechanical part and shortens the life of the motor. Although this problem seemed to be solved by applying core skew in the previous study, it was confirmed that the axial force caused by the axial leakage flux occurred in the maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) control section and the torque ripple was increased. Therefore, in this paper, a model that can apply symmetrical core skew and reduce axial force is proposed. First, the causes of axial force generated in previous studies were analyzed. Based on the analysis of these causes, a new symmetrical core skew structure was proposed, and its justification was verified through FEA.

articleTitle: Gray-Box Identification and Optimization of Reactor Inductance
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Analytical and numerical methods are widely used in the calculation of reactor inductance. However, it cannot meet the need of optimal design in terms of calculation accuracy and efficiency. An identifiable gray-box model for inductance calculation is established based on electromagnetic principles, and a sample data set of Inductance is generated by numerical simulation. The elite-retaining genetic algorithm is used to identify the parameters of the gray-box model, and the NSGA-III algorithm is utilized to perform the multi-objective optimization design of the reactor. After optimization, the quality and loss of the conductors are greatly reduced.

articleTitle: Isogeometric FEM-BEM coupling for magnetostatic problems using magnetic scalar potential
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: An original magnetic scalar potential FEM-BEM coupling based on isogeometric analysis is presented to address magnetostatic problems. The efficiency of the method is demonstrated on an academic problem and on a more complex multipatch geometry.

articleTitle: Impact of Nearby Lightnings on Wireless Power Transfer Ground Assembly
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Direct hits from Lighting Strikes (LS) are commonly recognized as dangerous events for open air installations, but also the much more frequent case of LS hitting nearby can cause overvoltage potentially damaging connected circuits, if not correctly protected. In this paper, adopting a hybrid formulation, we simulate the voltage induced at the terminals of a Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) ground coil by a LS hitting the ground nearby the system. The induced overvoltage has a non-negligible amplitude, depending on the distance of the hit, the tortuosity of the lighting channel, and the inclination of the coil with respect to the ground plane.

articleTitle: Torque Ripple Generation Mechanism of Induction Motors by Time and Space Harmonic Fields
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the generation mechanism of torque ripples in induction motors by using theoretical expression of torque ripples and electromagnetic field analysis, to obtain useful information of motor designs. It is revealed that the torque ripple generation mechanism of induction motors is quite different from that of synchronous motors. The proper stator/rotor slot combinations to reduce the torque ripple is also clarified.

articleTitle: Analytical Calculation of Electromagnetic Force of Surface-Mounted Permanent-Magnet Machine with Stator Notch using Subdomain Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, an analytical method based on subdo-main (SDM) is proposed to calculate open-circuit electromagnetic force of a surface-mounted permanent-magnet (SPM) machine with stator notch. SDM can precisely consider the effect of notch structure in magnetic field distributions rather than magnetic equivalent circuit (MEC) and conformal mapping (CM), and is faster than finite element methods (FEM). Therefore, the proposed method in this paper will help to predict electromagnetic force in the design stage. To verify the proposed method, the air-gap flux density obtained from FEM and the proposed method is compared. In addition, the effect of the stator notch on electromagnetic force regarding the depth and the width is studied through spatial and temporal harmonic analysis.

articleTitle: Examination of thickness evaluation of steel plate using DC bias magnetic field by 3D FEM analysis considering minor loop magnetic characteristics
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The thickness evaluation of steel plates in various plant structures is considered important for plant safety. In this paper, an electromagnetic inspection method that can evaluate steel plate thickness using a pulsed magnetic field was investigated. When a steady square-wave pulse magnetic field with DC bias was applied from the surface of the steel plate, the relationship between the leakage flux on the steel plate and plate thickness is investigated. In addition, the inspection principle was evaluated by electromagnetic field analysis considering eddy current and minor loop magnetic property of the steel plate and verification experiments.

articleTitle: Modeling and Optimization of aNew Magnetic Coupler Topology for DIPT Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The application of dynamical inductive power transfer (DIPT) systems is currently seen as one of the possible solutions to improve the autonomy of embedded power devices. In this context, electromagnetic field emissions play a crucial role in the system's design. In this paper, a new coil topology for magnetic couplers in DIPT systems is proposed, based on the use of adjacent current loops, which can improve the tradeoff between reducing the magnetic field emissions near the magnetic coupler and maintaining almost the same system's efficiency. In order to evaluate the topology's performance, finite element method simulations are carried out to determine the impact on the magnetic field emissions and the coupling coefficient. Finally, coil prototypes are developed in order to validate the results obtained by modeling.

articleTitle: The Criteria of Mitchell to Interpret Classical Radiation as Compton Scattering
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The principles of Machine Learning through the criteria of Mitchell are used to validate a concrete quantum-mechanics interpretation from a classical radiation scheme inside the framework of linear and nonlinear Compton scattering off a relativistic electron in a super-intense electromagnetic field.

articleTitle: A Novel Stator-PM Consequent-pole Dual Stator/Rotor Armature Winding Flux Modulated Machine for Multi-Torque Components
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel hybrid excitation alternate stator PM dual stator/rotor armature winding vernier machine with the DC-biased current. Due to the both armature windings and alternate stator PM interact with each other, this proposed machine contains six torque components. Compared with traditional stator permanent magnet machines and flux modulated machines, this machine makes full use of the space in rotor the cavity, giving full play to the flux modulation effect. This digest will introduce the topology of the machine and its operating principles, and then the electromagnetic characteristics will be analyzed by finite element analysis (FEA).

articleTitle: Computation of Torque using different non-conforming Interface Techniques
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this work, the influence of classical mortaring and Nitsche-type mortaring on the torque, calculated with the Maxwell stress tensor, is determined. The discretization of the air gap with quadrilateral and triangular elements as well as different non-conforming interface positions are investigated.

articleTitle: Multiscale Finite Element Formulations for the Eddy Current Problem in Open Magnetic Circuits
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The multiscale finite element method (MSFEM) has shown its high potential for the simulation of the eddy current problem in closed magnetic circuits. This work presents two formulations to extend the MSFEM to open magnetic circuits. To this end, a three dimensional eddy current problem with the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T,\Phi\text{-}\Phi$</tex> formulation and linear material relations has been studied. Numerical results demonstrate the accuracy of the presented methods.

articleTitle: Optimization of nonlinear iteration of the TLM-based finite element method and its application in electromagnetic field analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The solution procedure of the transmission line finite element method (TLM-FEM) is derived, and an optimized relaxation method is proposed to calculate the nonlinear part. TLM-FEM is a nonlinear algorithm that does not require repeatedly assembling the coefficient matrix, and the iterative process can be decomposed into a linear part and a nonlinear part. The LU decomposition of global matrix is performed on Graphical Processing Units (GPUs) by parallel technique in this paper. The proposed method has been applied to analyze the magnetic field of the long straight wire carrying current and a single phase transformer and its validity has been verified. The method can be used to analyze the electromagnetic field of large-scale electrical equipment.

articleTitle: Error Estimator for Continued Fraction Approximation of Linear Dynamical System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Cauer ladder network (CLN) method, which enables to approximate the eddy current problems by a Cauer circuit, can be generalized to the continued fraction approximation of a transfer function of a finite dimensional linear dynamical system. A new error estimator for the continued fraction approximation is proposed in the paper, which provides guaranteed upper bounds of the error of reduction.

articleTitle: Topology Optimization of Soft Magnetic Composites with Integer Programming
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Soft Magnetic Composites (SMCs) have huge application potential in electrical devices. With the development of additive manufacturing (AM), the properties of SMCs can be boosted. It is therefore required an optimization algorithm to design SMCs considering the AM capacity. Since the magnetic and loss properties of SMCs are highly sensitive to the shape evolution of the components, we introduce a topology optimization approach with integer programming. At each iteration, the components of the composite are determined with crisp boundary. This optimization algorithm converges rapidly because of the topology gradient and the optimal topology is reached.

articleTitle: Magneto-Thermal Analysis of a Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In the paper, a magneto-thermal analysis of a static Wireless Power Transfer System (WPTS) is performed. The analysis is based on the Finite Element Method coupling the two field problems. A prediction of the temperature increase in the car frame is accordingly calculated.

articleTitle: Anti-saturation Shielding Coil with Coupling Enhancement for Wireless EV Charging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The digest proposes a shielding coil featuring anti-saturation and coupling enhancement for wireless electric vehicle (EV) charging. The shielding coil is powered by the induced current and operates under reactive shielding mode using a tunable capacitor. By adjusting the connection of the dotted terminals, the direction of the current in each part of the shielding coil is designated. The coupling enhancement is achieved by the inner shielding coil carrying the current in-phase with the trans-mitting coil. The solenoids wounded on four edges of the ferrite generates opposing fluxes on corresponding edges to reduce the magnetic flux density in the ferrite to prevent saturation. The outer shielding coil carries current in a reversed direction of the transmitting current to reduce the leakage field outside of the target area. The proposed design significantly reduces the magnetic flux intensity in the ferrite to prevent saturation while not distinctively impact the coupling enhancement in one coil design.

articleTitle: Coupled 2-D FEM and 1-D Micromagnetic Model for Transverse Anisotropy Tape-Wound Magnetic Cores
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: We present a new approach for modeling high-frequency losses in transverse anisotropy magnetic tapes by solving a 1-D eddy-current problem coupled to a micromagnetic constitutive law. Contrary to earlier models, the model is derived using a magnetic flux-density conforming formulation. The model allows coupling the tape-level magnetization process to a 2-D finite element model for analyzing larger cores by homogenizing the tape layers.

articleTitle: Improvement of Magnetic Property Model Considering the Effect of Domain Area Variation on Magnetostatic Energy
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In order to improve the simulation accuracy of the domain energy hysteresis model, this paper proposes an improved magnetostatic energy formulation which can takes the effect of domain area variation into account. A magneto-optical Kerr microscope is employed to obtain the domain movement during magnetization, then the domain areas are extracted and converted into a correction coefficient in the magnetostatic energy. The validity of improved model is verified with the experimental data.

articleTitle: Computational Reconstruction of Dirac- Delta Function from Quantum Electrodynamics Rules
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: It is reconstructed the Dirac-Delta function exhibiting an interesting texture when the function is parametrized. For this end the well-known quantum electrodynamics rules are employed. Thus when the energy conservation is done then a closed form can be extracted and that is far away from its traditional meaning.

articleTitle: Convergence Analysis of the Cauer Ladder Network Method using Eigenfunction Expansion
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The Cauer ladder network (CLN) method is a model order reduction technique applicable to quasi-static electromagnetic field analysis. In this study, we derive an explicit formula for determining the error of the truncated transfer function and its upper bounds using the eigenvalues of Green's operator and the orthogonal polynomials associated with the basis functions for the CLN method.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Homogenized Finite Eddy Current Analysis using Recursive Convolution Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel method to effectively and accurately perform time-domain homogenized finite element analysis of the multi-turn coil windings. In this method, the macroscopic complex permeability is represented by the partial fraction and then the inverse Laplace transformation is performed by the recursive convolution method. It is shown that the results obtained by the present method are in good agreement with those obtained by the conventional FE analysis while the former works about 100 times faster than the latter.

articleTitle: Error Correction of Electromagnetic Force Calculation Using Nodal Force Method in Time Domain Eddy Current Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Accurate estimations of electromagnetic (EM) force is indispensable for evaluating the dynamics of the electrical machines. When the finite element method is applied to the EM field analysis, some numerical force calculation methods are used such as nodal force method. The calculation accuracy of the EM force is dependent on the several factors, namely, the magnitude of EM force, the resolution of the finite element mesh, distribution of the finite elements and so on. Recently, the authors proposed a method to improve the calculation accuracy of that using the error correction in the magnetostatic field. In this paper, the error correction method is extended to the force calculation in transient eddy current analysis.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Design Optimization of Conductive Shield for Eddy Current Systems Based on Multiple Continuum Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a design method to solve the multi-objective optimization problems of conductive shields in eddy current systems. The conductive shield is designed to protect the outer area of the system from the magnetic field while maintaining the system performance. The design sensitivities for the conductor shape corresponding to each objective function are calculated through the continuum method. The multi-objective design velocity is obtained from the multiple continuum sensitivity. The shape evolution is expressed using the level set method. The proposed method is verified by applying it to the design of conductive shields in a magnetic induction tomography system.

articleTitle: Magnetic Flux Density Calculation Accuracy Improvement Of Edge Finite Element Based On Superconvergent Patch Recovery Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, the Superconvergent Patch Recovery method (SPR) is applied to the electromagnetic field calculation problem. On the basis of the double curl equation of vector magnetic potential, the magnetic flux density is solved by the edge finite element method using the tetrahedral mesh. According to the Superconvergent Patch Recovery technology of finite element method, all elements around the certain element are formed into element group. By the interpolation of the superconvergence point field intensity in the element, the calculation accuracy of magnetic flux density is improved.

articleTitle: A New Dual Eddy-current Solver for Enhanced Accuracy of Global Quantities-Numerical Observations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Calculation of Tubular Permanent Magnet Linear Oscillation Actuator Considering Corrected Air Gap Permeance
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Tubular permanent magnet linear oscillation actuators (TPMLOA), with the simple structure and convenient control, have been paid extensive attention in the field of compressors and industry applications. In this paper, an electromagnetic calculation method of the TPMLOA is proposed. Firstly, a novel topology of the TPMLOA is introduced. Then, based on the radially laminated stator, the actual air gap permeance is derived by the flux tube method. Finally, the electromagnetic characteristic of the TPMLOA is analyzed by 2-D finite-element analysis (FEA) considering the corrected air gap permeance, and the results is compared with the 3-D FEA results. Additionally, for verifying the accuracy of the calculated results, a prototype of the TPMLOA is manufactured and tested.

articleTitle: Shape Optimization of mmWave Band Chipless RFID Tag Composed of Metasurface Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents shape optimization of chipless RFID tags composed of metasurface polarizer. Chipless RFID is susceptible to ambient influences because data is read at the backscatter wave resonance frequency of the tag. We propose and optimize a chipless RFID tag that introduces a metasurface that converts polarization to reduce the influence of disturbance. The optimized chipless RFID tag was found to have a polarization conversion efficiency of −0.56 dB.

articleTitle: A stress-dependent energy-based magnetic hysteresis model
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The effect of mechanical stress on magnetic hysteresis is modeled by an association of an energy-based magnetic hysteresis model in a vector-play form and a reversible simplified multiscale approach. A methodology for the identification of stress-dependent dissipation parameters is proposed. The main characteristics of the magnetic quantities and losses are captured by the model when compared to measurements, with some discrepancies on the shape of the hysteresis loop.

articleTitle: An Anisotropic Vector Play Model and Its Application to Magnetization Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: An anisotropic vector play model is constructed by the superposition of scalar play models. An analytical identification method for uniaxially anisotropic term is derived. Computed BH loops accurately reconstruct measured anisotropic hysteretic properties of non-oriented silicon steel sheet. Its application to a magnetization analysis improves the prediction accuracy of stress dependent loss property.

articleTitle: Analytical Modeling and Optimization of a Single-sided High Temperature Superconducting Linear Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, an improved analytical model is presented for calculating the performance of single-sided linear induction motor that primary windings are made of high temperature superconductor (HTS). The analytic model based on accurate subdomain, which the electromagnetic state of the superconductor can be taken into account, for predicting the magnetic field and analyzing the structural parameters on performance in HTS SLIM. As compared with the conventional analytic model, the accuracy of the proposed model, respecting the constraints linked to the physical and mechanical properties of the considered HTS tape, is observably improved. Finally, the finite element analysis (FEA) is used to verify the analytic model and compare it with the experimental results obtained from the prototype of HTS SLIM.

articleTitle: A New Arc Flux Modulated Machine with Hybrid Permanent Magnet Arrangement
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a new arc flux modulated machine with hybrid permanent magnet (PM) arrangement (HPM-AFMM) for drive of large-diameter telescopes. The proposed HPM-AFMM using hybrid PM arrangements can perform the double flux-modulation effect to increase torque density. The proposed HPM-AFMM combines the flux modulated PM machine and arc PM machine, which incorporates the benefits of high torque density, strong robustness and low cost. The structure and the operation principle of the HPM-AFMM are presented. The electromagnetic performances of HPM-AFMM are comprehensively investigated using finite element analysis.

articleTitle: B-H Curve Tracing by Magnetic Contact Force
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a B-H curve tracing method for material by magnetic contact force. In general, material data used in electrical devices are measured by the Epstein frame and VSM. However, the Epstein frame is difficult to measure in the high magnetic field area, and the VSM is expensive. The proposed method in this paper tracks the magnetic flux density and magnetic field strength inside the sample by measuring the force of the magnetic contact force sensor. Low-cost miniaturization is possible in a new way that is different from the existing method. The proposed method is explained in principle through a simple model and demonstrated through simulation.

articleTitle: Losses Calculation In Carbon Fiber Composite Materials Using Model Order Reduction Coupled With Domain Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The domain decomposition method is applied to simulate the local losses to do the induction thermography in carbon fiber reinforced polymer. This context will present optimized simulation by domain decomposition method with model order reduction method and the appropriate choice of convergence condition which can reduce the computational time and keep the accuracy.

articleTitle: Stochastic algorithm for optimal layer arrangement in a multilayer material for magnetic shielding
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This study presents a new method of combining the layers of magnetic materials and conductive materials for the elaboration of an optimal thin multilayer magnetic shielding for a given frequency range. The method consists in using genetic algorithms coupled with a finite element modeling tool for the choice of the thicknesses and the order of the layers within the multilayer allowing to obtain the optimal multilayer magnetic shield. This method allows to study the impact of the number of layers, the thickness, and the position of the layers on the shielding effectiveness of planar multilayer magnetic shields.

articleTitle: Circulating Current Suppression Method for 18-Slot 16-Pole Permanent Magnet Machine with Transposition Armature Winding Configuration
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) with concentrated winding, an imbalance of the strand induced voltage caused by the slot flux leakage might result in a heavy circulating current. The circulating current in the multi-strand winding causes the uneven distribution of strand current, which increases the copper loss and consequently decreases the system efficiency. This paper firstly introduces the generation mechanism of circulating current in an 18-slot 16-pole PMSM. Then a transposition winding configuration is proposed to suppress the circulating current in a 110kW 18-slot 16-pole PMSM. The transposition winding configuration is analyzed and compared with two accurate winding placements in terms of strand current distribution, copper loss and manufacturing process. The analysis results indicate that the transposition winding configuration can suppress the circulating current, which is validated by the efficiency measurement of the 110kW prototype.

articleTitle: Hybrid Method for Reducing Shaft Voltage Considering AC Copper Loss for IPMSM with Hairpin Winding
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid method that combines both analytical and finite-element methods to reduce shaft voltage (SV) considering AC copper loss. The proposed method consists of two stages. The first stage is a determination of design variables through the sensitivity analysis and the second one is an optimal design using a parasitic equivalent capacitance (PEC) and a finite-element method (FEM). To check the validity of the proposed method, it is applied to the design optimization of an interior permanent magnet synchronous motor. Also, the SV result gained by the PEC method is compared with that obtained by FEM.

articleTitle: Hot Spot Driven Physics-informed Neural Network via Special Designed Quantity of Interest applied to Magneto-thermal Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNN) have been widely used and achieved some good results in the field of computational electromagnetism. In this work, a hot spot driven physics-informed neural network (PINN) is proposed for magneto-thermal analysis. A loss function is specially designed, which takes the hot spot as the quantity of interest (QOI), for both its location and its temperature value. Besides, the influence of the QOI on the hyperparameter is investigated to ensure the convergence of the PINN. Numerical experiments show that the proposed approach can significantly improve the accuracy of the predicted temperature of the hot spots.

articleTitle: A Novel Family of Inductance Matrix Compression Techniques
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Integral methods for the solution of eddy current problems are very appealing since they avoid the meshing of the insulating regions. Yet, their main shortcoming is that they require the assembly and storage of a fully populated stiffness matrix K. To reduce the memory footprint and to enable a fast matrix construction, low-rank approximations techniques-like the Adaptive Cross Approximation (ACA)-have been considered a major breakthrough in the field. This paper presents a novel family of compression techniques that is enabled by a novel explicit factorization of the inductance matrix. Such a novel family exhibits orders of magnitude speedup and memory consumption with respect to state-of-the-art techniques. In particular, the aim of this paper is to compare for the first time the memory occupation, computation time and accuracy of the solution obtained with different compression techniques.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of a new Permanent Magnet Machine with Flux-intensifying property
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In electric vehicles, the multi driving conditions put forward new requirements on the speed regulation range of its motor. Hence, a new IPM synchronous machine owns the characteristics of flux-intensifying effect are proposed in this paper. Based on this, the operation characteristics of the machine are emphasized. and the relationship between flux-intensifying characteristics and machine performance is studied in detail. Finally, the possibility of applying this kind of machine to EVs under multiple operating conditions is verified by finite element analysis.

articleTitle: Topology-Parameter Hybrid Optimization of Skewed Permanent Magnet Motor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a topology-parameter hybrid optimization of a permanent magnet motor with a step-skewed rotor. This optimization simultaneously performs the topology optimization of the core shape and parameter optimization of the skew angle. The simultaneous optimization is shown to provide the optimized motors superior over those obtained by the sequential optimization. Moreover, the optimized shape is shown robust with respect to the variation in the skew angle.

articleTitle: Transient Modelling of Corrosion Protection Systems with BEM-Electrical Circuit Hybrid Model
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Modelling of corrosion protection systems in seawater is classically based on Boundary Element Method (BEM) with a limitation to static studies. This paper presents an original transient approach hybridizing BEM and circuit solving, enabling the modelling of more complex system and interface phenomena.

articleTitle: Modeling of magnetoelectric effects in composite structures by FEM-BEM coupling
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a coupling of the Finite Element Method (FEM) and the Boundary Element Method (BEM) is used to model the behaviour of magnetoelectric effects in composite structures. This coupling of numerical methods makes it possible not to have to consider a free domain, and thus to use a single mesh for the magnetic, mechanical and electrical problems. This results in a consequent reduction of the number of unknowns which is accompanied by shorter computation times compared to a classical FEM approach. A mixed magnetic vector potential-reduced magnetic scalar potential formulation is used for the magnetic problem, and classical FEM formulations are used for electrical and mechanical problems. The resulting global algebraic system is solved by a block Gauss-Seidel solver.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Axial-Flux Modular Interior Permanent Magnet Machines with Yokeless and Segmented Armature
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel axial-flux modular interior permanent magnet (MIPM) machine with the yokeless and segmented armature (YASA). The modeling was performed by coupling the magnet magnetomotive force (MMF) of PMs with the permeance of air-gap to predict the working harmonics. Then, the influence of rotor pole numbers on the electromagnetic performance of the proposed machine is analyzed in detail. Finally, a conventional YASA machine with surface-mounted PM (SPM) is compared to reveal the merits of the proposed machine in terms of PM eddy current loss and irreversible demagnetization using 3-D finite-element analysis (FEA).

articleTitle: Analysis of a Novel Fault-Tolerant Multi-Tooth Flux-Switching Permanent Magnet Machine
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Flux-switching permanent-magnet machines with multi-tooth stator structure have attracted wide attention due to their advantages of high torque density and high efficiency. Based on it, a fault-tolerant multi-tooth flux-switching permanent-magnet machine (FTMFSPM) is proposed and compared to the conventional fault-tolerant flux-switching permanent-magnet (FTFSPM) machine. In order to evaluate the electromagnetic performance of proposed FTMFSPM machine, a comparison of the electromagnetic performance of proposed FTMFSPM machine and conventional FTFSPM machine is conducted by finite-element analysis (FEA), and the FEA-predicted results indicate that the proposed FTMFSPM machine exhibits better electromagnetic performances than FTFSPM machine, such as more sinusoidal and larger back EMF, high average torque, smaller torque ripple, higher self-inductance and lower mutual-inductance.

articleTitle: Reduced-Order Model Based on POD and Polynomial Fitting for Parametric Magnetostatic Field Problem
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The reduced-order model (ROM) has been utilized in many problems to take the place of the full-order model, which is usually derived from the finite element analysis. The ROM based on the combined proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) and polynomial fitting method is proposed in this paper to study the nonlinear magnetostatic problem with parameterized excitation current. The leave one out cross validation (LOOCV) is investigated to determine the degree of the fitting polynomial to reduce the probability of overfitting.

articleTitle: System-Level Robust Design Optimization of a Permanent Magnet Motor Under Design Parameter Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In the presence of design parameter uncertainties, a system-level robust design optimization (RDO) method for a permanent magnet motor is proposed to enhance steady and dynamic performances of the whole motor drive system. To achieve the goal, the influence of individual motor parameters on transient system responses is investigated essentially. Then material characteristic of each motor component due to the operating temperature fluctuation is examined as well. Finally, a conventionally customized motor drive system is fully simulated based on the finite element method, and the motor is optimized by the univariate dimension reduction method (uDRM).

articleTitle: GPU-Accelerated Field Simulation of HVAC Gas Insulated Lines
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The knowledge of the electric field distribution in gas insulated lines (GIL) under alternating currents (AC) is essen-tial to ensure a reliable operation of the system. This can be deter-mined by numerical simulation and requires a fast linear solver for the Poisson problem. Utilizing the AmgX library on NVIDIA A100 graphic processing units (GPUs) to solve a Poisson system of linear equations with millions of degrees of freedom enables a so-lution time up to 0.11 s.

articleTitle: Parasitic Capacitance Calculations for Influences of Direct-Oil Cooling System in Traction Motor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This study proposes the analytical method for the influences of parasitic capacitance and shaft voltage for the direct-oil system in traction motors. First, the parasitic capacitances are calculated according to the dielectric constant of insulating materials, including the cooling oil. Then, the calcu1ated parasitic capacitances are used to construct an equivalent circuit considering the shaft voltage path of the traction motor. Finally, this study analyzes the parasitic capacitance and shaft voltage characteristics according to the cooling oil level using the proposed analytical method. It will be verified through finite element analysis and experiment.

articleTitle: The Method for Reducing Intrinsic Shaft Voltage by Skewed Slots in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper pays attention to a method to calculate the optimal skewed slots angles which can effectively reduce the intrinsic shaft voltage of permanent magnet synchronous motors(PMSMs). First, the analytical method designed the analytical model which focuses on the qualitative analysis of intrinsic shaft voltage with skewed slots. The analytical model can clearly calculate the optimal skewed slots angle which can reduce the shaft voltage to minimum. The finite element method is used to calculate the shaft voltage of 6-pole/9-slot PMSM and verify that skewed slots is an effective method to reduce intrinsic shaft voltage.

articleTitle: Model reduction of differential-algebraic equation systems using constructed spectral projectors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This contribution introduces linear differential-algebraic equation (DAE) systems and provides the explicit construction steps of spectral projectors for a DAE with index 1 or 2. Further, a interpolatory projection-based model order reduction technique using spectral projectors is applied to an electrical circuit to compute a reduced order model.

articleTitle: Optimal Design and Verification of Stacking-Hole in Transformer Core Based on Analysis of Magnetic-Fluid-Thermal Coupling
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The loss and local temperature of the transformer core increases due to the stacking hole. To minimize the impact of the hole, a novel shape of the hole is designed and proposed in this paper. The finite element method and the experimental method are used to verify the optimization effect of the proposed novel hole. Based on the finite element method, the model of the core with the hole is established to simulate and calculate the core loss of the transformer under no-load condition. Subsequently, the loss as heat source maps into the thermal field to establish the magnetic-thermal-fluid coupling model. Considering the dependence of temperature on material properties, the convective heat transfer process is simulated and the temperature rise is calculated. The impacts of the traditional hole and novel hole on the transformer performance are compared and analyzed. Based on the experimental method, the loss and local temperature rise caused by the traditional hole and novel hole are quantitatively measured and compared. The simulation and experimental results show that, compared to the core without the holes, the loss is increased by 10-15% due to the traditional holes, the loss caused by the novel holes increases by 3-6% and the maximum optimization of the loss is up to 11%. The core with novel holes achieves an excellent performance which is superior to the core with current holes.

articleTitle: Fast Topology Optimization of PM Motor Using Variational Autoencoder and Neural Networks with Dropout
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a fast topology optimization of a permanent magnet (PM) motor using variational autoencoder (VAE) and neural network (NN) with dropout. PM Motors generated through topology optimization are embedded into low-dimensional latent space using VAE. For high reliability, the properties of the motor generated from the latent space are evaluated by NN with Monte Carlo dropout. It is shown that the proposed method can provide very fast approximations of the Pareto solutions at good accuracy.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor for Eco-friendly ship using Hybrid ABC-SVM Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper investigates the best design of IPMSM for eco-friendly ships using a hybrid ABC-SVM algorithm (HAS). HAS is a multimodal optimization method capable of exploring several optimal solutions. HAS enhances navigation capability by combining the existing Artificial Bee Colony algorithm (ABC) with Support Vector Machine (SVM). In addition, hybridization with Simplex enables accurate and quick convergence on neighbor optimization at pointers discovered in ABC. In two test functions, the higher performance of the proposed algorithm is tested with conventional ABC, and the algorithm is applied to the optimal design of the IPMSM for the eco-friendly ship.

articleTitle: Torque Ripple Suppression Strategy Based on Field Current Segment Compensation for Doubly Salient Electro-magnetic Machine
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The cogging torque generated by field current and field inductance is the main reason for the severe torque ripple in doubly salient electro-magnetic machine (DSEM) systems. To reduce the torque ripple, especially the part caused by cogging torque, a field current segment compensation control method is proposed for DSEM systems. The components of torque and the influence factors of each component are analyzed. The effect of field current on torque ripple is analyzed and the control strategy of field current compensation is proposed to reduce the torque ripple caused by cogging torque. Simulation results verified the compensation for the torque gap in the commutation area and the effectiveness of torque ripple suppression of DSEM compared with conventional methods.

articleTitle: Design for Wide Operating Range of Vernier Permanent Magnet Machine with Two-Slot Coil Pitches
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the vernier permanent magnet machine (VPMM) with two-slot coil pitches suitable for direct-drive applications. In general, direct-drive applications demand a high torque, wide operation range and a high power factor. VPMM is well known as high torque machine at low speed, but its critical drawback is low power factor. This can be enhanced with two-slot coil pitches. In this study, our model attains high torque, flux weakening capability and loss characteristic is discussed in the study. Finally, electromagnetic performance optimization of the model chosen will be conducted through the one of the multi-objective optimization algorithm.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of Magnetic Force on Stator Core according to Material Modeling
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The validity of magnetic force calculation and loading method are important for NVH synthesis in numerical simulation due to difficulty in direct measurement of magnetic force in electric machines. In this paper, magnetic force on stator core according to material modelling are quantitatively investigated for several electric machines. 2D Time-stepping finite element magnetic simulations and Post-calculation for local magnetic force and input loading to mechanical analysis are carried out.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Rotor Topologies for Synchronous Reluctance Motor Based on Many-Objective Optimization
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, we report a new rotor topology of the reluctance synchronous motor (SynRM) with auxiliary flux barriers. In order to analyze the performance of the new topology, SynRM models with the auxiliary flux barriers are compared to traditional SynRM models. At this time, each model is optimized considering five characteristics: 1) specific power, 2) torque ripple, 3) efficiency, 4) total harmonic distortion of voltage, and 5) power factor. For the purpose of simultaneously optimizing the five characteristics, a many-objective optimization, NSGA-III, is applied. Moreover, the two-dimensional finite element method is employed for the precise simulation of the motor performance.

articleTitle: 2.5D Topology Optimization to Design Overlapping Winding in Multi-Phase Coreless Electrical Machine
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Coreless electric motors are gaining interest from the community as they have a larger power-to-weight ratio and a larger efficiency. The absence of iron slots leaves the winding space unobstructed. This enables the geometry of the coils to be skewed to overlap with their neighbors. Such arrangement provides better motor constant. This work proposes to establish some groundwork for the topology optimization of overlapping winding in multi-phase coreless motors. A 2.5D formulation of the density-based approach is proposed to enable the designed coils to span over two layers and spatially overlap with their neighbors, while keeping a limited computational cost. A novel interpolation scheme is also proposed to account for multi-phase winding while only designing one phase.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis using the Virtual Work Principle For 2D Magnetostatic Problems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The rise of shape and topology optimization techniques has opened new possibilities to find innovative designs for electromagnetic devices such as actuators or rotating machines.
