This paper provides an analytical sensitivity analysis for the magnetic force and torque based on the virtual work principle and suitable for those kinds of optimization.

articleTitle: Optimal Sensor Placement via Parameterized Background Data-Weak Method applied to Magnetostatic Problems including Anisotropy
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The need for electrical machines is growing in a wide range of applications nowadays, such as for energy production, automotive, marine, and medical equipment, etc. In most of these applications, reliability, efficiency, performance and operational safety are always critical issues, which implies that the monitoring and analysis during the operation of the equipment need to be strengthened. In general, more sensors can give higher accuracy for the estimated physical quantity. However, the system cost, complexity, and size of both system and sensor, as well as the electromagnetic interference can eventually limit the sensor placement. Optimization of the number and the location of the sensors in the monitoring system is one key point to improve system performance, as well as reduce system cost. In this work, an optimal sensor placement strategy is proposed for the application of magnetostatic problems, where the anisotropy of the material is considered. Our development is principally based on the parameterized background data-weak (PBDW) method. The feasibility and efficiency of the proposed approach are illustrated by the numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Wide-Speed-Range Performances of Rotor Structural Deformation of V-Shaped IPMSM in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: With the rapid development of electric vehicle market, its production and sales continue to increase, and the quality of electric vehicles determines its future development. To enhance the performances of the interior permanent magnet motor (IPMSM), this paper proposes solutions of structural deformation on the V-shaped permanent magnet (PM) rotor. Novel structures are designed based on a double V-shaped IPMSM model. Then the influence of the deformed V-shaped PM rotor is investigated, including the efficiency and the power factor under the wide-speed range required by electric vehicles. Via comparing numerical analysis and experimental data, the performances of different structures of the IPMSM are obtained, with which useful solutions are achieved to reduce the rare-earth materials in electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Power Factor Analysis of IPMSM with Low Fractional Slots per Pole per Phase
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper analyzes power factor (PF) characteristics of motors with low fractional slots per pole per phase with respect to d-q inductances and flux linkage. The negative effect of asynchronous operation caused by different number of poles between stator and rotor is analyzed, in terms of PF. Moreover, optimization for high PF is carried out to analyze improved configurations according to number of slots per pole per phase.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Iterative-Direct Solver Based on Fast Multipole Method for Efficient Finite Element-Boundary Element Coupling Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The coupling of FEM-BEM in electromagnetic modeling can be beneficial for problems involving open boundary or motion, or more general for problems with complex geometry. However, its efficiency is limited because of the dense block introduced by the BEM discretization. In this work, a hybrid iterative-direct solver based on fast multipole method is proposed and implemented for efficient FEM-BEM coupling to accelerate the computational procedure. The computational time and memory usage can be reduced to linear complexity with the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Power Transformer Characterization and Design Optimization Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Power Transformers are essential part of all AC Power Grids. This work proposes a characterization and design optimization environment for Power Transformers to increase efficiency while decreasing core volume. It utilizes a Finite-Element State-Space models in conjunction with Artificial Neural Networks, and Particle Swarm Optimization. A case study of a 42 MVA, 118/13.8kV distribution power transformer was conducted and transformer performance characteristics were compared to test data for verification. Next, the optimization environment was used to improve transformer efficiency and decrease its volume. In addition, the Taguchi orthogonal arrays method was used to reduce the computational costs.

articleTitle: Study of Small-world Spiking Neural Network Based on Anti-interference Ability against Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The study of robustness contributes to improving the neural information processing ability of brain-like models. However, the effect of topological structures of brain-like models on anti-interference ability has not been clarified. In this study, integrating the Izhikevich neuron model, the synaptic plasticity model, and the small-world network, a small-world spiking neural network (SWSNN) is constructed. Then, the anti-interference ability of the SWSNN is assessed based on two anti-interference indicators under AC magnetic field. Finally, the anti-interference performance of SNNs with different topologies is compared. The simulation results consistently verify that: (i) The SWSNN has anti-interference ability, and the intrinsic factor of anti-interference ability is the synaptic plasticity. (ii) In terms of anti-interference performance, the SWSNN outperforms the scale-free SNN, which hints that topological structure affects the anti-interference ability at the level of performance.

articleTitle: Induction Heating Analysis with Cauer Ladder Network Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper uses the Lanczos algorithm to derive a Cauer ladder network for heat transfer analysis. The obtained equivalent circuit is called the Cauer-I type equivalent circuit and consists of thermal inductance and thermal resistance. Reapplying the Lanczos algorithm to this Cauer-I type equivalent circuit equation yields a Cauer-II type equivalent circuit composed of thermal capacitors and resistors, similarly to a general thermal circuit.

articleTitle: Core Loss Analysis of Soft Magnetic Composites Based on 3D Modeling under Non-sinusoidal Excitation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Based on the existing soft magnetic composite (SMC) finite element models, three-dimensional(3D) finite element simulation models of SMC single particle and magnetic ring sample were established in this paper. In view of the fact that the existing finite element models do not take into account the effect of harmonics on the hysteresis loss of SMC, based on the hysteresis loss calculation formula of Bertotti loss separation theory, an improved expression of hysteresis loss coefficient is derived by introducing the correction factor of loss coefficient. And it is applied to the model so that the model can be used to calculate the magnetic core loss under non-sinusoidal excitation. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed model are verified by comparing with experimental results.

articleTitle: A Computationally Cheap Error Estimator for the 3D Eddy Current Problem Using a MSFEM Approach Based on the A-Formulation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The multiscale finite element method allows for the efficient calculation of eddy currents in laminated cores. This paper presents an error estimator which can be calculated on the same coarse mesh as the multiscale solution, making it computationally cheap while providing an accurate estimation of the error for both linear and nonlinear materials. Because of its local structure, this estimator enables adaptive mesh refinement.

articleTitle: Dual Magnetostatic Formulations for Problems having General Boundary Conditions
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Dual formulations are more reliable and accurate in computing energy-related global quantities such as inductances and capacitances by providing the upper and lower bounds of the true values of the global energy-related quantities. Existing dual formulations adopt different variables belongs to totally different finite element spaces and thus will produce totally different algebraic matrix equations to be solved separately. In this work, two recently proposed dual formulations for open region problems where the coefficient matrices are exactly the same, are generalized to solve problems with general boundary conditions for cases with reduced full model or other scenarios. Two numerical examples are computed to show the accuracy of the proposed formulations.

articleTitle: Design of High Power Density Spindle Motor Based on Multi-objective Optimization Considering Moment of Inertia
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Reducing energy consumption in spindle system has received attention from many researchers because of rising awareness of environment impact in manufacturing process. Moment of inertia is linked closely to energy consumption with motor efficiency and power density. In this paper, we present optimal design of spindle motor based on reducing moment of inertia for saving energy consumption. IPMSM is applied to the spindle motor instead of IM. Multi-objective optimization of IPMSM is conducted. Moment of inertia, power density and cost of energy consumption are objective functions of optimization. PM area is selected as optimization boundary because of high PM cost.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Model Order Reduction of a Variable Reluctance Stepper Motor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The parameterized Cauer ladder network (CLN), which is a recently developed nonlinear model order reduction method, was applied to the analysis of a variable reluctance stepper motor. The transient motor characteristics calculated using the parameterized CLN were in good agreement with those obtained using finite element analysis. Additionally, we showed that a nonlinear analysis of the step-input response can be conducted.

articleTitle: A Novel Methodology for Topology Optimization Considering Manufacturing Errors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Manufacturing errors (ME) are ubiquitous and inevitable in product engineering manufacturing. A novel methodology based on morphological operations and random filed (MORF) is proposed for the discrete-variable-based topology optimization procedures to consider MEs. Morphological operations are firstly introduced to generate the geometrical variation. Moreover, the diameter of the structuring element in the morphological operations is set as the output of the random field function. Using the proposed approach, MORF is capable of quantifying spatially nonuniform ME rigorously. The numerical result has validated the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Physics-Based Model and Its Solution Methodology for Hysteresis Mobile-Ionic Dielectrics
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A physics-based model and the corresponding solution methodology for the mobile-ionic (MI) dielectrics exhibiting Q-V(Charge-Voltage) hysteresis behaviors are proposed based on ion drift-diffusion (IDD) equations coupling with Poisson's equation. The proposed model captures the dynamic distribution of mobile ions' concentrations within dielectric along the external electric field. The accuracy of the proposed model is validated by comparing the computed results with the experimental ones.

articleTitle: Topology Optimization of Electric Machines Based on Homeomorphic Mapping
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In order to improve the performance of the motors, topology optimization (TO) is often applied in the motor design process. This paper investigates a method of TO which is based on the homeomorphic mapping. In this method, the basic shapes of the object components are placed in the design area and deformed by the homeomorphic mappings. TO is achieved by optimizing the parameters of the homeomorphic mappings. The homeomorphic mapping represents deformation without splits or self-intersections, it is able to avoid complicated shapes. The optimization results confirmed that this method provides the uncomplicated optimal shape.

articleTitle: All-in-One Magnetic Bearing in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor by Halbach Array
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: When the magnetic bearing is coupled to the motor, the size of the motor is greatly increased as a separate structure that controls the shaft from the outside of the rotor. In this paper, a method is proposed to minimize the size increase of the entire system by inserting the existing magnetic bearing into the rotor through the halbach arrangement. The halbach arrangement makes it possible to eliminate the magnetic circuit inside the rotor, so the rotor back yoke can be minimized. As the rotor back yoke is minimized, the inner space of the rotor can be secured, and the existing separate magnetic bearing is inserted inside the rotor. The all-in-one magnetic bearing in which the magnetic bearing and the rotor are integrated controls the rotor from the inside of the shaft, and it is possible to replace the existing separate magnetic bearing. A 16-pole 24-slot surface permanent magnet synchronous motor was selected as an analysis model. Through finite element analysis, the size of torque and bearing force was maximized, and the ripple of each component was designed to be minimized. Through the new magnetic bearing motor presented in this paper, it is possible to utilize the advantages of magnetic bearings and to minimize the size and weight.

articleTitle: Zeroization of Cogging Torque of Permanent Magnet Machines by Optimizing Rotor Surface Shape: Comparison between Surface and Interior Types
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the mechanism of cogging torque reduction by optimizing the rotor surface of permanent magnet synchronous machines. The optimizations of both the surface and interior permanent magnet machines are carried out. It is clarified that the cogging torques of both the machines can be reduced to be nearly zero by optimizing the rotor surfaces, whereas the mechanisms of cogging torque reduction of these machines are completely different from each other.

articleTitle: Computation of the Electromagnetic Fields of Overhead Power Lines with Boundary Elements
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a numerical approach for computing the electromagnetic fields of overhead power lines by means of the boundary element method. It is based on boundary integral equation, which allows the unbounded problem to be entirely defined at its boundary, and therefore reduces the number of variables required to solve it. The proposed methodology can be used to find the potential gradients not only over the surface of the conductors, but also anywhere of interest in space. The paper also deals with analyzing the influence of grounding wires and the influence of different types of boundary elements on the field distributions. The boundary domain is discretized in both constant and linear elements, and comparisons against analytical results show accurate approximations for the field distributions, even for small computational domains and lower order elements. Besides, the grounding wires, generally disregarded, are shown to have an actual impact on the field distributions, and can be easily taken into account by using the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Time Domain Integral Operator for an Offset Impulse Radiating Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this work a closed time-domain formulation was developed to analyze offset IRA (Impulse Radiating Antennas) satellite dishes responses. Such antennas present more complex geometry than reflector parabolic antennas fed at the focus. For this reason, the formulation studied here has more extensive expressions. At first, expressions for the field radiated by the offset reflector in the frequency domain were revised. They were obtained by approximations of geometric optics (GO) and the aperture method. Following, the inverse Laplace transform was applied to those expressions, which allowed obtaining radiation expressions in the time domain, which were used to determine a unit step temporal response.

articleTitle: A Hall-based Modified Finite Position Set-Phase Locked Loop for Sensorless Control of PMSM
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a hall-based modified FPS-PLL algorithm for sensorless control of surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). The modified algorithm utilizes a permanent magnet (PM) flux linkage observer to increase the calculation accuracy, and hall sensors to reduce the calculation amounts. Simulations have been investigated to test the performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Investigation on Behavior Model of PMSMs Considering AC Copper Losses with Cauer Circuit
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Conventional behavior models treat the armature impedance as a DC resistance and this approximation highly underestimates the copper loss at higher frequencies. In this paper the impedance is represented by the Cauer circuit to consider the frequency dependency of the impedance and hence to improve the accuracy of loss calculation. A permanent magnet synchronous motor is calculated using the proposed method and the results are compared with FEM results to clarify its usefulness.

articleTitle: Multiphysics Analysis and Power Density Improvement for Traction Motor by Applying CNT-Cu Winding
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Recent research trends on the electric machine are focusing on not only motor topologies, but also motor component materials. The application of carbon nanotube composite material to the motor is one of the ways to bring innovative changes in motor power generation. Compared to copper, carbon nanotube-copper (CNT-Cu) composite conductor has high conductivity at high temperature, low temperature coefficient of resistance, excellent thermal properties, and also advantages of having low weight. In this study, the power density improvement of the motor for the electric vehicle was carried out by applying the CNT-Cu composite winding. Furthermore, the effect of CNT-Cu windings on the motor was demonstrated by conducting an AC copper loss analysis and calculating through the equivalent circuit based motor thermal analysis.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Eddy Currents in Laminations, Multiscale Finite Element Method, Harmonic Balance Method and Model Order Reduction
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A computationally feasible methodology has been studied for the eddy current problem (ECP) in laminated iron cores of electrical devices. The multiscale finite element method (MSFEM) based on the magnetic vector potential has been exploited using the harmonic balance method (HBM) and a simple model order reduction (MOR) method. Several simulations by means of a numerical problem are presented demonstrating efficiency and accuracy of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Research on Kernel Feature Construction and Integration Method of Power Transformer under Incomplete Information
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The digital transformation strategy puts forward higher requirements on the information support system of the power system, and it also points out the direction for the operation and maintenance of key equipment such as large power transformers. First of all, this paper explains the power transformer holographic data perception architecture, key technologies, and analysis methods from a multi-parameter perspective. Then, based on actual cases, establishing a power transformer information decision table according to equipment components and fault types, and the “kernel” characteristic fingerprint of the power transformer was obtained. Secondly, by analyzing the distribution of the “kernel” feature indicators, a Task Flow Graph-Tasks (TFG-T) data integration architecture and fusion model based on the cloud-pipe-edge-terminal architecture is proposed. The data transmission and integration were described in detail under this model. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed method is verified by simulation analysis of the arithmetic example.

articleTitle: Research on Finite Element Equivalent Models and Analysis of Motion Characteristics of Magnetic Screw for Wave Energy Conversion
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: As a linear rotary actuator with high force density and high energy conversion efficiency, magnetic screw (MS) is being studied for application in the field of wave energy conversion (WEC). In order to further study, optimize and improve the energy conversion performance of the MS, and because the permanent magnet (PM) of the MS is helical, it is necessary to conduct three-dimensional (3D) simulation modeling to study its internal magnetic field distribution and force. However, the calculation and solution of the 3D simulation model not only requires high hardware conditions of the computer, but also has so much grid points and takes a long time to calculate. Therefore, it is necessary to simplify the 3D model and establish a finite element equivalent model (EM). On the basis of fully studying the basic structure and working principle of the MS, the thrust equivalent model and the torque equivalent model of the MS are proposed, including 3D EM and 2D EM, respectively. In addition, the motion equations of MS are also established according to the EM study on the motion characteristics of MS. Finally, finite element simulation results are used to verify the effectiveness of EM and its significance for future work.

articleTitle: An Efficient Implementation of Inverted Preisach Model Combined with Reversible Magnetization Component and Improved Distribution Function
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, according to the problem that the classical Preisach hysteresis model cannot accurately describe the reversible magnetization in the process of material magnetization, the reversible magnetization component is calculated by using the experimental data of reversible permeability by analyzing the reversible magnetization process. At the same time, aiming at the problem that the distribution function is difficult to determine in irreversible magnetization, the inverted Preisach model based on the inverted switch operator and improved distribution function is proposed. By using the inverted switch hysteresis operator, the parametric distribution function is obtained. By coupling the waveform factor in the distribution function, the identification of hysteresis loop under low magnetic density is strengthened. The parameters of parametric distribution function are obtained by identifying the limit hysteresis loop by velocity-controlled particle swarm optimization (VCPSO) algorithm. In the numerical calculation, the amplitude correction coefficient in the discrete formula is extracted by the basic magnetization curve. Finally, the validity and accuracy of the hysteresis model are verified by experimental comparison.

articleTitle: A Computational Efficient Method for Modelling of Circulating Current Loss in Electrical Machines With Stranded Windings
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a computational efficient method for evaluating the circulating current between parallel strands in electrical machines with stranded windings. Firstly, the lumped parameter circuit model is introduced, and then the key parameters, namely slot leakage inductances, are calculated by the proposed non-strand finite element model. Finally, the accuracy of the method is validated by FEM simulations.

articleTitle: Topology Optimization of Electromagnetic Devices with Movable Magnetic Path under Fixed Amount of Materials
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a new topology optimization method for electromagnetic devices with movable magnetic path under the fixed amount of materials. The amount is preserved strictly on the basis of a new hybrid encoding (binary and per-mutation encoding). A new variable magnetic path is successfully obtained by optimizing the material distributions several times.

articleTitle: Optimization of SynRM for High Efficiency Considering Airgap Flux Density Shape
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents the rotor optimization to improve the motor efficiency for air ventilation system in railway station. SynRM creates a salient ratio through a barrier inside the rotor, and electrical characteristics can be improved through magnitude of this ratio. However, depending on the location and shape of the barrier, electromagnetic output characteristic(torque, efficiency, and ripple) may change due to saturation level and permeance variance even though the salient ratio is the same. Therefore, in this paper, design variable capable of affecting saturation and permeance variance such as the position of the barrier and the salient ratio is analyzed, and the optimal shape that can obtain the best output under the constraint condition is derived through the RSM(Response Surface Method). Finally, the validity of this study was verified through FEA simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: Model Order Reduction of a Cage Induction Motor with Skewed Rotor Slots Using Multiport Cauer Ladder Network Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A method for efficiently deriving a reduced order model of a cage induction motor (IM) with skewed rotor slots is proposed based on the Cauer ladder network (CLN) method. Several formulations of the CLN method for the skewed rotor are presented, in which space harmonics included in the air-gap flux density waveform are differently treated. Finally, the effectiveness of the developed methods was verified from the standpoints of computational accuracy and cost by applying it to a practical cage IM with skewed rotor slots.

articleTitle: A Study on the Shape of Polar Anisotropic Molding Yoke to Reduce the Dead Zone of a Ring Bonded Magnet
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A ring magnet attached under the safety window motor is used for detecting the position of the window with a hall sensor. A dead zone that the magnetic flux is weak appears between the poles of the ring bonded magnet and the larger the angle of the dead zone, the more difficult it is to detect the precise position of window. In this study, the shape of polar anisotropic molding yoke with a magnetic flux concentration structure is proposed to reduce the range of the dead zone. The results were analyzed through finite element analysis and the final model was selected by analyzing the inner and outer teeth thickness of the teeth of the molding yoke as design variables. The prototype of the final model was manufactured, and the validity of the analysis result was verified.

articleTitle: Optimization design for an electromagnetic energy harvester based on Halbach array
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Energy harvester is a practical solution to provide energy to the wireless sensor network continuously. However, it is still suffered with low output due to energy form environment is subtle and dispersive. An electromagnetic energy harvester based on Halbach array is proposed and optimized to improve the output in this paper. To enhance the magnetic flux density on the side of the coil, Halbach array is designed to take place of one whole piece of magnet. To maximum the changing rate of the magnetic flux density, an improved whale optimization algorithm is developed to optimize the Halbach array-based energy harvester. The numerical results demonstrate the optimized electromagnetic energy harvester with halbach array can promote the output.

articleTitle: A Novel Derivative Free Methodology for Topology Optimization
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Most existing methods for topology optimization update the material distribution iteratively based on the derivative information. However, the calculation of gradient is of low accuracy and even unavailable in some cases. To this end, this paper proposes a novel derivative free methodology for TO based on affine transformations and Boolean operations. Specifically, the proposed method selects the basic structures to constitute a new topology. Affine transformations and Boolean operations are employed to represent the evolvement and the way of combinations of the basic structures. The numerical result has validated the proposed method.

articleTitle: Investigation of Teeth Number on Stator Poles in Flux-switching Permanent Magnet Machine Considering the Magnet Utilization
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, based on the conventional flux-switching permanent magnet (PM) (FSPM), the influence of the teeth number on the stator pole in the FSPM machine is studied. In order to compare the electromagnetic performance between2-, 4-, 6-, 8-, 10-teeth/stator pole FSPM machines, the optimal combination of stator pole and rotor teeth for five same stator poles but different stator teeth FSPM machines is investigated. Then, the influence of the placement of the PMs of the FSPM machines is analyzed, Finally, the five FSPM machines are quantitatively compared by finite element analysis (FEA). The FEA-predicted results reveal that the torque contributed by the per-unit PMs volume of the FSPM machines also increases when the teeth number on the stator pole grows, which can improve the magnet utilization of the motor.

articleTitle: Vector Nodal Meshless Method for 3D Magnetostatic Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Traditional meshless methods use scalar-based functions and therefore, present difficulties in approximating vector fields. The Vector Nodal Meshless Method (VNMM) constructs its approximations using shape functions based on edges whose length tends to zero in order to reproduce vector fields. The VNMM has been applied to solve two-dimensional electromagnetic problems [1]. This paper presents the construction of VNMM functions for use in three dimensions vectorial problems. The formulation is tested using a magnetostatic shielding problem with analytical solution.

articleTitle: Model order reduction techniques for linear differential-algebraic equations applied to semi-discretized eddy current model
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The generation of reduced order models describing the input-output behavior of linear quasi-stationary electromagnetic field problems is in many applications of particular interest, e.g. in the field of wireless power transfer. This contribution demonstrates the construction of a differential-algebraic equation system to describe a given single-input single-output behavior of an eddy current model which is essential for a broad range of model order reduction techniques.

articleTitle: From Topology Optimization to 3D Printing of an Electromagnetic Core
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This communication presents a bridge between topology optimization and additive manufacturing. On the one hand, it presents an algorithm that considers the design variables as binary and then solves the problem by linear programming to optimize a ferromagnetic core. On the other hand, a 3D printing process is developed to manufacture the shapes obtained by topology optimization, which are then submitted to electrical measurements.

articleTitle: Extended Finite Element Method for Calculation of Eddy Currents at High Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The extended finite element method is used for calculating eddy currents at high frequencies, which reduces the number of unknowns in conductive materials at these frequencies. In this study, a two-dimensional model is analyzed numerically, and the solution is compared with the numerical solution obtained by the conventional finite element method.

articleTitle: Modeling of Excess Loss in Non-Oriented Electrical Steel Sheet Considering Grain Orientation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A modeling method of excess loss taking account of random grain orientation in non-oriented electrical steel sheet is proposed. In the proposed method, the steel sheet is modeled with grains having random orientation and parallel magnetic domain structure. The anisotropic magnetic characteristics due to the parallel domain structure is considered in each grain. The initial BH curve and excess loss obtained from the proposed model are compared with those of actual non-oriented steel sheets. It is shown that the initial BH curve can be reproduced in high flux density region, but the excess loss can be reproduced in low flux density region.

articleTitle: Effect of Flux Barriers on Short-Circuit Current and Braking Torque in Dual Three-Phase PM Machine
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper investigates the influence of stator flux barriers on the short-circuit current (SCC) and braking torque of dual three-phase permanent magnet (PM) synchronous machine. In order to achieve high output torque and fault-tolerant capability, the flux barriers are commonly introduced on the armature teeth. Firstly, the SCC is analytically derived and it is found that the SCC amplitude is proportional to the PM flux linkage and inversely proportional to the self-inductance. The braking torque is proportional to the square of the PM flux linkage and inversely proportional to the self-inductance. Then, the equivalent magnetic circuit model of flux barriers is established. Its influence on flux linkage and inductance is analyzed, and the improvement mechanism of output torque and fault tolerance is revealed. Furthermore, the flux barrier width are optimized by finite element analysis and the theoretical analysis is verified. Finally, the experiments on the prototype machine are carried out for the validation.

articleTitle: Residual Flux Density Measurement Method of the Single-Phase Transformer Based on Phase Difference
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: When the power transformer is energized under no-load conditions, the residual flux will accelerate the saturation of the core, and generated magnetizing inrush current will cause many harms to the power grid. To determine the residual flux in the transformer core with a closed magnetic circuit structure, this paper proposes a method for measuring the residual flux of the transformer based on the phase difference between the test voltage and the transient current. The finite element method is used to model and analyze the core to be tested and obtain an empirical formula for calculating the based on the simulation results. Finally, an experimental measurement platform was built, and the measurement results verified the feasibility and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Slot/Pole Relationship and Winding Configuration of Dual Winding Dual PM Flux Modulated Machines
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes four slot/pole combinations of dual winding and dual PM flux modulated machine (DWDPM). The main structure of DWDPM is that armature windings and permanent magnets are positioned on both the stator and rotor sides. When adopting unique slot/pole combination, the stator windings and the rotor windings can interact, respectively, with the stator PMs and the rotor PMs to output average torque. The electromagnetic performance of the proposed models is analyzed and compared according to finite element analysis (FEA). The result shows that the DWDPM having close slot and pole combinations can output more torque and have lower torque ripple.

articleTitle: Accelerated Frequency Domain Field Simulations of Linear Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Linear induction motors (LIMs) represent an elegant modern solution for future transportation, motion control, and linear automation systems. As opposed to their rotational counterparts, simulation based design and optimization of LIMs is still an open research subject due to their specific geometrical-and electromagnetic features. The time domain FEM eddy current analysis is a widely used tool for analyzing LIMs capable of taking into account a dynamically moving rail and a coupling of the motor with its power supplying electric circuit. To replace the computationally intensive time domain FEM analysis of LIMs the paper suggests a frequency domain FEM analysis and a concept of an effective rail conductivity for taking into account the rail movement. The numerical results of the prosed method are compared against the classical time domain approach and a high level of agreement has been found.

articleTitle: Finite Element Modeling and DWT Analysis of Power Transformer Interturn Faults
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: As one of the most common types of faults inside transformers, interturn short-circuit faults seriously threaten the safe operation of the bulk power grid. In this digest, power transformer interturn faults were investigated by coupling the transformer finite element model and the external circuits. As typical fault cases, interturn faults inside a three-phase two-winding power transformer were simulated, and discrete wavelet transforms was adopted accordingly to extract the characteristics of the terminal currents. The results show that the wavelet coefficients exhibited significant differences between normal operation and interturn short-circuit faults. Due to the nonlinear characteristics of arc in insulation oil, periodic spikes appear in the detail signal, corresponding to the zero crossing of arc current.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of a Permanent Magnet Claw Pole Machine with Hybrid Cores
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Permanent magnet claw pole machine (PMCPM) is a new type of transverse flux permanent magnet machine (TFPMM). Due to its special structure, its stator core is usually made by soft magnetic composite (SMC) materials. Based on PMCPM with SMC cores, a new PMCPM with hybrid cores is proposed in this paper. The hybrid core is produced by the combination of silicon sheet cores and SMC cores. Compared with the PMCPM with SMC cores, the PMCPM with hybrid cores has higher average torque and efficiency. However, as the permeability of silicon sheets is higher than that of SMC material and it replaced the SMC in part of stator yoke, the power factor of PMCPM with hybrid cores is lower than that with SMC cores. For performance evaluation, 3-D finite element method (FEM) is adopted, and the PMCPM with SMC cores is used as the benchmark comparison.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network Based Electro-Mechanical Optimization of Electric Motors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this contribution the authors use a Deep Neural Network based approach for the optimization of an electric motor, taking into account both electromagnetic and mechanical constraints, i.e. approaching the problem from the multiphysics point of view.

articleTitle: A Study on the Impedance Method for Offline Inter-tum Fault Diagnosis of Induction Motor Using Co-analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, the impedance of IM is analyzed according to the electrical connection instead of the mechanical connection. The electrical connection is equal the mechanical connection according to voltage vector position. The inter-turn fault diagnosis algorithm is proposed according to the voltage vector position. Co-analysis of a finite element analysis (FEA) and control circuit simulation is performed to verify the proposed inter-turn fault diagnosis algorithm. Furthermore, IM and terminal box are manufactured, and the experiment is performed to verify the inter-turn fault diagnosis algorithm.

articleTitle: Quantitative Comparison of Flux Regulation Capability of Integrated-Induction-Based Hybrid Excitation Machines with Spoke-Type and Consequent-Pole PM Rotors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In recent years, hybrid excitation machine (HEM) drawn much attention due to their preferred flux regulation than permanent magnet (PM) machine. The integrated-induction-based HEM (II-HEM) achieves both the brushless excitation and flexible flux regulation while the high space utilization is obtained. This paper aims to quantitative comparison of flux regulation capability between the novel II-HEM adopting consequent-pole PM rotor and the conventional counterparts adopting spoke-type PM rotor. The flux regulation principle of the two II-HEMs are revealed based on equivalent magnetic circuit model, and validated by finite-element (FE) method. Then, the regulation coefficient kf is defined for evaluating the flux regulation capability, in which the actual saturation effect is considered. It is demonstrated that the novel II-HEM with consequent-pole PM rotor obtains better flux regulation capability than the conventional one.

articleTitle: Data-driven sparse discovery of hysteresis models for piezoelectric actuators
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a new approach to model hysteresis in piezoelectric actuators based on recent advances in sparsity promoting machine learning methods. While sparse regression has successfully modelled several phenomena in sci-ence and engineering, its performance in modelling the nonlinear hysteresis behaviour in piezoelectric materials is still unexplored. This study applies the sequential threshold least-squares (STLSQ) algorithm to discover the governing hysteresis expressed in the form of a dynamical system. It is found that a parsimonious model governing the dynamics is extracted from a large candidate library, which predicts the hysteresis efficiently with less than le-3 relative percent error, demonstrating the algorithm's efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on Field-Circuit Coupled Model of EBE Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A field-circuit strong coupled model of element-by-element finite element method (EBE-FEM) is derived, and the mathematical model is presented in this paper. EBE-FEM is a parallel algorithm in which large-scale global computations are decomposed into mutually independent local computations without assembling the global coefficient matrix. The proposed method has been applied to analyze the magnetic field and current of transformer, and the validity has been verified. The method can be applied to the field-circuit coupled analysis of large-scale power equipment.

articleTitle: Efficient Recursive Convolution Schemes for the Accurate FDTD Modeling of Graphene Interband Contribution via Complex Conjugate Pairs
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The accurate numerical modeling of graphene surface conductivity due to the interband contribution is presented in this paper. In particular, a precise vector-fitting technique is utilized for the decomposition of the analytical conductivity function into complex conjugate pairs. Then, a proper recursive convolution scheme is developed to efficiently incorporate the prior approximation in the conventional FDTD algorithm.

articleTitle: Three-Phase Six-State Strategy for Active Rectifier in Doubly Salient Electromagnetic Generator System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: To improve the output power of the doubly salient electromagnetic generator, an active rectifier three-phase six-state (3P6S) strategy is proposed by turning on the IGBTs on the upper arm in advance with an angle on the basis of the advanced angle control. The AAC uses the flat-top zones of phase inductance by turning on the corresponding IGBTs on the upper and lower arms with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\alpha}$</tex> in advance to accelerate the commutation processes compared with the angular position control. While the 3P6S strategy uses the freewheeling process of phase current to increase the current of the phase about to start work in advance and further improves the output power. Compared with the conventional three-phase three-state strategies, the proposed 3P6S strategy raises the phase current and improves the output power. The performance of the 3P6S strategy is verified by finite-element analyses.

articleTitle: Influence of Supporting Failure on Magnetic-structural Displacement for Power Transformer Windings under Short Circuit Fault
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: When the power transformer vibrates during operation and withstands short-circuit electromagnetic force many times, the insulation support structure of the transformer winding will appear asymmetric phenomenon. At this time, the winding is again affected by short-circuit electromagnetic force, transformer winding will occur more serious displacement, bulge and collapse. In this paper, a three-dimensional magnetic-structure coupling model is established, and the magnetic flux density and electromagnetic force density of power transformer windings under short-circuit current are calculated by finite element method (FEM). Taking the short-circuit current as the independent variable and the winding displacement as the dependent variable, the electromagnetic field and structural field are simulated and analyzed by Ansys Workbench software to obtain the winding displacement results.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Algorithm Based on NSGA-II and MOPSO for Multi-objective Designs of Electromagnetic Devices
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid algorithm is proposed by combining the NSGA-II with MOPSO algorithm. The original NSGA-II is improved by adopting dynamical selection of crossover and mutation operators. The performance of the proposed hybrid algorithm is verified using standard test functions and it is applied to the multi-objective optimization benchmark problem TEAM 22. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed hybrid algorithm.

articleTitle: An Improved PSO based Methodology to Extract Frequency-Dependent Stray Parameters of High Order Distribute Circuit Models
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In an advanced electronic and electrical system, the transient process may finish in an extremely small time span. Consequently, the stray parameters of the system play a dominant role in this transient process, and a high order distributed circuit model is more rigorous for simulating the corresponding transient. However, it will be difficult to apply the existing approaches to determine the frequency-dependent model parameters in simulating such a wide frequency band response. To address this issue, an improved Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) based methodology to extract frequency-dependent stray parameters of high order distribute circuit models of an advanced electronic and electrical system is proposed and validated by experimental studies.

articleTitle: Force Ripple Minimization Design for Consequent Pole Permanent Magnet Linear Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper focuses on the force ripple minimization of consequent pole permanent magnet linear synchronous motor (CP-PMLSM). By using arc teeth without tooth shoe, CP-PMLSM is investigated in detail by extensive finite element analysis (FEA). With Taguchi parameters method, the geometry of end teeth and auxiliary teeth is optimized to reduce the force ripple, and the optimal combination of parameters can be obtained. the contrasting result between the initial and the optimized PMLSM shows that the force ripple is suppressed to a quite low value in all load conditions by the aforesaid procedure.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Automatic Design of Permanent Magnet Motor Using Monte Carlo Tree Search
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel multi-objective design method of permanent magnet (PM) motor using Mote Carlo Tree Search (MCTS). In this method, the whole machine structure of a PM motor, such as the number of poles and magnet configuration, and detailed magnetic structure are simultaneously optimized. The proposed method is shown to give Pareto solutions that consist of PM motors with different number of poles and magnet configuration.

articleTitle: Parasitic Capacitance Modeling for Toroidal Inductor Using Multi-Axial Sliced Finite Element Model
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents an application of a multi-axial sliced finite-element (FE) model to predict parasitic capacitance of a ferrite core toroidal inductor. A time-harmonic 2-D FE problem is solved in several slices taken axially and radially from a 3-D toroidal inductor, and the precomputed capacitances between the conductor regions are considered to model the displacement currents. The frequency-dependent complex permeability and complex permittivity of the core are taken into consideration for characterizing the inductor over a frequency range of 10 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{kHz}$</tex> to 1 MHz. In particular, the self-resonance frequency of the inductor is studied. The validation of computed results is made against measurements.

articleTitle: Reduced Order Simulation by Proper Generalized Decomposition of a Synchronous Generator with Passive Rectifier
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The simulation of electrical machines connected to electronic circuits by a field circuit coupling enables the consideration of the electric circuit with active components and its influence on the machine. In the computation of the electric domain, the machine is represented by linearized inductances and electromotive force, but after a particular number of simulations of the electronic system, the electromagnetic simulation is repeated to consider the change in the magnetic field, which states a finite-element (FE) problem. To decrease the computational effort of the FE problem the Proper Generalized Decomposition (PGD) is employed, to reduce the Degrees of Freedom (DOF). The PGD process can be distinguished into two stages: In a first step, the offline phase, the reduced order model is enriched with modes. In the second step, the online phase, the modes, which contain the information about the system in different load conditions have to be assessed to compute characteristic values, such as inductances or torque. By employing the PGD in a numerical weak coupling, the computational effort of the Finite Element computations is reduced.

articleTitle: Scale Reduction for Rapid Prototyping of Wireless Power Transfer System for Electrical vehicules
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, the scale reduction method is applied to a 3D model of a wireless inductive charging system for electric vehicles for its rapid prototyping and simulation. The co-simulation between a 3D FEM model of the wireless power transfer system (WPT) and the power electronic part is studied and in particular thanks to the scale reduction method. A preliminary comparison between the measurement and the FEM model of the coupling coefficient on the one hand and the computation time on the other hand highlights the high potential of the scale reduction method for prototyping and simulation of a realistic WPT system.

articleTitle: A Numerical Twin Model for the Coupled Field Analysis of TEAM Workshop Problem 36
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A numerical twin model for the magneto-thermal analysis of an induction heating device is proposed. The nonlinearity of magnetic permeability against temperature - which characterizes the workpiece - is captured by the model, while the use of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), trained by a number of finite-element analyses, makes it possible to reconstruct the temperature field map in the workpiece region. TEAM problem 36 is recalled as the case study.

articleTitle: Continuum Sensitivity Analysis for Shape optimization of Transient Eddy Current System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a shape sensitivity analysis for the transient eddy current system. The continuum shape sensitivity of the transient eddy current system is derived by using the material derivative concept and the adjoint variable technique. In the continuum shape sensitivity analysis, the state variable equation is an initial-value problem to be solved forward in time. In contrast, the adjoint variable equation is a terminal-value problem, which is solved backward in time. With the state and adjoint variables, the design velocity of the shape sensitivity formula is evaluated and coupled with the level set equation to represent the deforming geometry. A numerical example having the known solution is tested to show the feasibility of the derived sensitivity formula.

articleTitle: Compound Magnetic Detection Method for Receiver Positioning of Wide-area Dynamic Wireless Charging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This digest presents a compound magnetic position detection method for the wide-area dynamic wireless charging that can realize dynamic positioning of two-dimension. To achieve accurate detection, electromagnetic sensors are arranged on the transmitter (Tx) coils and a permanent magnet is installed on the receiver (Rx) to measure the horizontal distance between the sensors and the Rx. Meanwhile, the coupling law is investigated to recognize the rough position of the Rx, thereby enhancing the accuracy. The designed detection method coordinates the switchover between the Tx coils and optimizes the performance of the wide-area DWPT system in a cost-effective manner.

articleTitle: Near Field Regulation Method of Electric Field Coupling and Magnetic Field Coupling
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The transmission of Poynting vector in wireless power transmission system is one of the essential laws of energy exchange in space. This paper gives its energy transmission mechanism in space and the distribution law of Poynting vector. At the same time, the coil inductance effect and capacitance effect in the actual work process are explored. The proportional coefficient of system energy transmission is given through theoretical calculation, and the regulation of energy proportion is realized through the key factors in the regulation coefficient, and It is verified by experiments.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Characteristics Analysis of High Power Superconducting Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents an electromagnetic analysis of 40 MW high temperature superconducting (HTS) synchronous motor. Combining electric resistivity variation of stator winding in cryogenic environment and critical current of second generation YBCO superconducting tape which is as rotor exciting coil, the characteristics with non-ferromagnetic stator teeth and semi-ferromagnetic stator teeth of the HTS synchronous motor are explored. The influence of different stator winding currents on eddy current losses of the rotor copper shielding sleeve are preliminarily discussed. The model and calculation results were verified from the points of view of electromagnetic parameters, critical current, eddy current loss and electromagnetic torque, respectively. This study has certain reference significance for the research and development of high-power HTS motors.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling for Induced Eddy Current Calculation on a Non-uniform Mesh
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The eddy current is one of the unavoidable effects in the electrically conductive parts of electrical machines. Its calculation is not easily achieved. In particular, the induced current developed by the primary eddy current is generated, and it increases the computational complexity. In order to study the induced eddy current, this paper uses the finite difference method (FDM) as the numerical method, and the finite-difference (FD) stencil is applied to the curl, div., and the discrete Laplace operator. In addition, this paper applies some methods to reduce the numerical error the calculation. There are two general numerical errors: round-off errors by rounding of decimal values, and truncation error by using approximations in the mathematical process. Each error can be reduced by applying a higher order FD scheme, and a smaller increment of the local discretisation in the structure. Especially, to evaluate the eddy currents at the edges of the structure, the non-uniform mesh is proposed, which leads to a reduction of the computing costs as well. The numerical results gained with a non-uniform mesh is compared to the results reached by a commercial FEM tool to demonstrate the accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Novel MSFEM Approach Based on the A-Formulation for Eddy Currents in Iron Sheets
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The multiscale finite element method has been shown to be an efficient tool in the simulation of eddy currents in laminated cores. This paper presents a novel multiscale formulation which corrects some shortcomings of the current method, giving a more physically meaningful solution that is more accurate than the current formulation while also requiring less degrees of freedom.

articleTitle: Field Control Method for Coupling Efficiency Improvement of Two-dimensional Dynamic Wireless Charging System with Multiple Transmitter Coils
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The digest presents a current distribution strategy for two-dimensional dynamic wireless charging (DWC) system with four transmitter (Tx) coils. This strategy regulates the electromagnetic field generated by multiple Tx coils along with migration of receiver (Rx) coil, which improves the coupling efficiency drastically. In the actual operation, a neural network (NN) is adopted to adjust the currents at primary side, guaranteeing a fast and accurate response. For devices with random position, this digest provides an efficient controlling method of the charging platform, supporting wide-range dynamic wireless power supply and high-speed responding calculation.

articleTitle: A Study on Combination of Number of Poles and Slots for Uniform Control of Magnetic Bearing
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: An integrated magnetic bearing structure can be designed that secures the space inside the rotor core as a space for inserting the magnetic bearing by applying the halva arrangement. In this case, since the bearing exists inside the rotor, the bearing magnetic flux for controlling the rotor position is affected by the magnetic field of the permanent magnet and the rotating magnetic field of the phase winding of the stator. At this time, in a specific combination of the number of pole slots, the arrangement of the windings of the stator facing the bearing teeth appears asymmetrically for each bearing phase. In this paper, for more linear control, the formula for the number of stator pole slots and the number of bearing teeth to eliminate structurally generated force asymmetry was presented, and the formula was verified by comparative analysis of force waveforms for each axis. The validity of the proposed model was verified using the finite element method.

articleTitle: ADRC Control of Electromagnetic Vibration in In-wheel Motor Considering Air Gap Eccentricity
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In view of the influence of electromagnetic vibration caused by road random excitation and unbalanced electromagnetic excitation on in-wheel motor, a vibration suppression method based on active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) is proposed. The road random excitation and electromagnetic excitation generated by the motor itself are regarded as total disturbances for unified observation compensation control. The results show, that the proposed control strategy has a better inhibitory effect on the eccentric electromagnetic vibration generated during the operation of the in-wheel motor.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on Iron Loss and Motor Performance of annealed and unannealed Amorphous Magnetic Material based Permanent Magnet Motor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, iron loss, back EMF, electromagnetic torque, and motor efficiency of unannealed amorphous magnetic material (UAMM) and annealed amorphous magnetic material (AAMM) based interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) are compared and evaluated. Firstly, magnetic properties of strips and wire-cutting cores of UAMM, annealed amorphous magnetic material (AAMM) and non-oriented silicon steel (NOSS) were measured, compared and evaluated. And then, IPMSMs using stator core of UAMM, AAMM and NOSS were numerical calculated and experimental tested respectively. The experimental results exhibit that IPMSM using stator core of UAMM at rated working point can offer approximately 1.17% and 2.09% higher efficiency compared with using stator core of AAMM and NOSS, respectively.

articleTitle: An Equivalent Circuit of Induction Motor Coupled to a Power Inverter Using Numerical Co-simulation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this work a three phase induction motor (IM) and power inverter co-simulation is developed. The IM is represented by a 2D finite element model(FEM). Whereas, the power inverter model is developed in state space equation using equivalent circuits. The co-simulation strategy between the field model and the power inverter is through equivalent circuit of the IM with feedback of lumped parameters and mechanical variables. Also, an analysis of the variation of parameters during the transitory stage and discussion of types of co-simulation are presented.

articleTitle: Transient Overvoltage Calculation of Dry-type Air-core Reactor with Complex Topology
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, the equivalent circuits of dry-type hollow reactor with complex topology are established by dividing the turns and layers. Considering the nonlinearity of the voltage distribution of reactor windings at high frequencies, the simulated and measured results of lightning impulse voltage distribution are compared. The circuit parameters are calculated and extracted using empirical formulas and finite element analysis software, and equivalent circuit models are obtained using different equivalent methods for capacitance parameters. The waveform distribution of the voltage between windings under lightning impulse is simulated, and the difference between the voltage gradient waveforms under different models and the measured results is compared.

articleTitle: Robust Design Method for Surface-Mounted Permanent Magnet Motor with Two-slot Pitches Winding Considering Eccentricity
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Eccentricity is a frequent problem caused by uncertainty in the manufacturing process. Since eccentricity makes that the air gap is not uniform, torque ripple can increase. Using two-slot pitches winding can decrease the influence of eccentricity with high winding factor. This paper reports a step-by-step robust design method for eccentricity by applying two-slot pitches winding. Before we start, the advantages of two-slot pitches considering eccentricity is analyzed. Then, the eccentricity robust design method is reported in 4 steps. First, an optimal slot configuration with two-slot pitches winding is searched to improve motor characteristics considering eccentricity. Second, general optimization at uneccentric state is performed. Third, design variables which are sensitive to back electromotive force (EMF) is selected because the variation of each phase back EMF is affected to eccentricity. Finally, optimization for the robust design is conducted by a kriging surrogate model. As a verification about the proposed robust design, the result of comparison between the uneccentric model and the eccentric model is shown. For evaluating characteristics of the motor, the finite element analysis is used considering static eccentricity.

articleTitle: Non-probabilistic Reliability-based Robust Design Optimization of Electrical Machines Considering Interval Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: An efficient non-probabilistic reliability-based robust optimization method (NRBRDO) is proposed by incorporating the decoupling strategy and interval analysis approach for the electromagnetic machines with interval uncertainties. The double-loop NRBRDO problem is decoupled into a series of sequential loops, including the robust optimization based on the Chebyshev polynomial expansion and the reliability analysis based on the performance measure approach. The result of a benchmark design optimization problem of blushless direct current wheel motor is presented. Furthermore, the optimization results are compared with the deterministic optimization and the robust optimization to verify the developed method.

articleTitle: Topology Optimization of an Electromagnet Manipulator for 3D Uniform Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Magnetic manipulation is a method used for biomedical applications to remotely control micro-robots in a contactless manner. The electromagnet manipulator should control a magnetic field with 3 degrees of freedom inside a region of interest. In various case studies, this field is the result of the superposition of three decoupled uniform magnetic fields. Each of them is individually generated by a different pair of Helmholtz coils. Such arrangement requires the pairs to be nested within each other, inevitably reducing the size of the working area, degrading the performance and the integration of the whole system. The proposed work aims to design a novel electromagnetic manipulator with the help of computational design, to explore beyond the Helmholtz coils arrangement. A topology optimization framework is developed for this purpose. It investigates the distribution of coils that achieves the largest working area, while keeping the different degrees of freedom balanced.

articleTitle: Finite Element Computation of the Direct Magneto-Mechanical Coupling Considering Anisotropy of Magnetostriction
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: When the solution region contains magnetostrictive materials such as electrical steels, a coupled magneto-mechanical solution is often required. In this paper, the finite element formulation of the direct magneto-mechanical coupling is derived based on the variational method, and the method of dealing with the anisotropy of magnetostriction in electrical steel material is proposed. The core deformation of a transformer model is computed using the magnetic-mechanical coupling program.

articleTitle: Circuit Model for Fast Computational Analysis of RWPT Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE 20th Biennial Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This work proposes a circuit model to calculate the current along printed coils used in resonant wireless power transmission systems. The proposed formulation is based on the Neumann formula for calculating the mutual inductance between coils, and due to the generality of this approach, it can be applied to more complex structures such as metasurfaces. Finally, this formulation is used to calculate the scattering parameters of the entire system, making it possible to evaluate its wireless power transfer efficiency. The results obtained agree with the general behavior obtained from electromagnetic simulations in commercial software, with a low error and a reduction in computational time of almost three orders of magnitude.
